Can your team confirm whether this is a config change on Redwood's side or something on our end? This is causing elevated pages and the exec team is asking for a short timeline for mitigation.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Ruiz

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 07 Oct 2028 10:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 jump — production impact this morning

Thanks Evelyn — tracing confirms request backlog ahead of the inference workers. Two plausible, not mutually exclusive causes: 1) per-tenant concurrency cap enforced more strictly after an internal policy change, and 2) a KV cache miss storm causing more tokens to be served from full model rather than cached prefixes, increasing per-request CPU/GPU usage and reducing throughput.

Immediate mitigation I can kick off now:
- Temporarily raise Polaris' concurrency cap from 40 -> 80 in the routing tier (will allow more parallel requests).
- Enable short-lived bypass on prefix cache checks for their tenant to cold-start a smaller set of warmed contexts (risks: higher cost).

I can run both; recommend raising the cap first (fast) and monitor 15 minutes.

—Marcus
SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 07 Oct 2028 10:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 jump — production impact this morning

I checked the per-tenant policy engine logs — we pushed a global tightening of soft concurrency limits yesterday at 23:40 to reduce cross-tenant interference in noisy workloads. The policy should be permissive, but for some tenants with bursty request patterns the enforcement moved from best-effort to hard caps because of a bug in the cooldown path. That matches Polaris' symptom set.

Action: I'll patch the cooldown logic (small change) and push a hotfix to the policy service; ETA ~60 mins. In the meantime Marcus' temporary cap increase is the right call.

—Jonas
Policy & Routing Lead

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@polarishealth.com>, Polaris SRE <sre@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 07 Oct 2028 10:41:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 jump — production impact this morning

Marta — quick update from our side: we see the same tail in queue wait time and have identified two contributing factors: a stricter-than-intended enforcement of per-tenant concurrency limits after a policy tweak, and a cache miss surge that increased execution load.

Immediate steps we're taking (watching now):
- Temporarily raising Polaris' concurrency cap (40 -> 80) — expected to reduce queue waits within ~5–15 minutes.
- Jonas is deploying a patch to the policy cooldown path to stop hard-capping bursty tenants — ETA ~60 minutes.
- Marcus is enabling a short-lived cache-warming bypass to reduce cold-start overhead (monitoring for cost impact).

We'll monitor telemetry and follow up in 30 minutes with p95/p99 graphs and an ETA for a permanent fix. If you have any preferences for rollback or you'd rather we take traffic off the Dedicated pool while we patch, say so and we can coordinate.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts checkout. I'll provide an exec summary once we have the 30-min results.

—Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 07 Oct 2028 16:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Exec note: Polaris incident — summary and next steps

Team / Marta,

Thanks for the speedy triage. Brief summary for executives:
- Incident: p99 latency regression (to ~2.9s) and small error-rate increase impacting ~8% of Polaris checkout requests starting 08:50 EDT.
- Root cause (confirmed): unintended hard enforcement of per-tenant concurrency caps after a recent policy tightening; secondary contributor was a KV cache miss surge increasing execution time per request.
- Immediate mitigation completed: temporary concurrency cap increase for Polaris and policy cooldown patch deployed. Early monitoring shows p99 back to ~480ms and error rate returning to baseline.
- Next steps:
  1) Post-mortem with timeline and RCA (Evelyn to lead) — due EOD tomorrow.
  2) Permanent fix: add stronger unit tests around policy cooldown and throttle rollback, and add a gradual enforcement flag for policy changes. (Owner: Jonas)
  3) Platform improvements: better prefix caching telemetry and an automated per-tenant warming path for cold-starts (Owner: Marcus).
  4) Customer communications: provide Polaris a short exec brief and credits for their impacted window (Account + Finance coordination).

I'll prepare a short exec note for our leadership and Polaris' execs; Marissa please prepare a customer-facing paragraph.

—Aditya Rao
VP, Customer Reliability
